item.title: Nasaroa becomes first in family to attain postgraduate qualification
item.description: 26-year-old Semisi Nasaroa has reached a major milestone after becoming the first in his family to attain a postgraduate qualification while balancing full-time work and part-time studies. Nasaroa, who is from Lekutulevu, Vaturova in Cakaudrove, graduated from the University of the South Pacific with a Postgraduate Diploma in Professional Accounting.
item.content:encoded:
26-year-old Semisi Nasaroa has reached a major milestone after becoming the first in his family to attain a postgraduate qualification while balancing full-time work and part-time studies.

Nasaroa, who is from Lekutulevu, Vaturova in Cakaudrove, graduated from the University of the South Pacific with a Postgraduate Diploma in Professional Accounting.

INSERT: Nasaroa on achievement 13th Sept

He says his parents have been his greatest supporters, standing by him from day one through to his graduation.

Nasaroa is a senior auditor at Ernst & Young and says the journey was challenging, with time management being one of his biggest difficulties.

He says balancing deadlines from his full-time job with his part-time studies was not easy, but he remained determined and continued pushing forward.

item.title: $5,000 assistance opens new opportunities for Cobia youths
item.description: Young people on Cobia Island are expected to benefit from new opportunities in sports and small business activities after the Cobia Island Youth Club received items worth around $5,000. The assistance includes tents and various sporting equipment, which the club says will help boost youth participation in sports and provide ways to generate income.
item.content:encoded:
Young people on Cobia Island are expected to benefit from new opportunities in sports and small business activities after the Cobia Island Youth Club received items worth around $5,000.

The assistance includes tents and various sporting equipment, which the club says will help boost youth participation in sports and provide ways to generate income.

Club spokesperson Josaia Cagituevei says the youths are grateful for the support and receiving the items is a proud and happy moment for them.

Cagituevei says the tents can be hired out for community and other functions, providing an opportunity for the youth club to generate income.

He says the sporting equipment will also encourage more young people to participate in sports.

He has thanked the Government for its support towards the youths and the Cobia Island community.

Cagituevei says the assistance will help empower young people by giving them opportunities to stay involved in sports while also supporting them economically.
